title: The Mathieu Property over Fields of Characteristic Zero: Classification and Ground-Field Obstructions
summary: Classifies the Mathieu–Zhao property for split reductive actions in characteristic zero, including spaces without rational points. Gives further real-closed, compact Hausdorff and ground-field obstruction theorems.
publication_boundary: Companion to Hexagon 2611.00556v1. The compact exceptional real products and the general anisotropic nonsplit classification remain open. The quadratic-complement classification is a separate manuscript.
abstract:
Let \(K\) be a field of characteristic zero and \(X\) an affine geometrically
homogeneous space of a group \(G\) with split reductive identity component.
The normalized Reynolds kernel on \(K[X]\) is Mathieu--Zhao if and only if
\([G^\circ,G^\circ]\) acts trivially. A single active split \(\SL_2\) already
gives a fixed marked counterexample for a connected reductive acting group.
Both results allow \(X(K)=\varnothing\). The proof transfers witnesses along
principal orbits and specializes marked-moment recurrences over the ground
field. We also classify connected reductive groups and compact adjoint
semisimple torsors over real closed fields, and representative functions
on compact Hausdorff homogeneous spaces. A long-root subgroup gives a
further obstruction when a split central torus acts alongside an active
compact factor of rank at least two.

hexagon_submission.abstract: We classify the Mathieu–Zhao property for affine geometrically homogeneous spaces over every field of characteristic zero when the acting group has split reductive identity component. The criterion is trivial action of the connected derived group. One active split SL2 already gives a counterexample for a connected reductive acting group, even for a space with no rational point. The proof transfers rank-one witnesses along principal orbits and specializes a recurrence while preserving infinitely many marked moments. We also classify connected reductive groups and compact adjoint semisimple torsors over real closed fields, and representative functions on compact Hausdorff homogeneous spaces. A long-root obstruction applies when a split central torus acts nontrivially alongside an active compact factor of rank at least two.
